Reigate and Banstead's population increased by around 13,000 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 150,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Reigate and Banstead increased by 9.4%, from just over 137,800 in 2011 to around 150,800 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Reigate and Banstead was home to around 8.3 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 7.6 in 2011. This area was among the top 40% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Reigate and Banstead than across the South East

Median age in Reigate and Banstead

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Reigate and Banstead increased by one year, from 40 to 41 years of age.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 4,000 (an increase of 15.7%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by around 450 (6.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.0 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Reigate and Banstead

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Reigate and Banstead, but fell across the South East.

In Reigate and Banstead, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 23.9% in 2011 to 24.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 21.0% to 20.6%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Reigate and Banstead fell from 19.3% to 16.8%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 6.6% to 7.0%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Reigate and Banstead increased by 0.9 percentage points

Health in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 52.6% of Reigate and Banstead residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 49.8% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 34.9% to 33.2%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Reigate and Banstead residents describing their health as "very bad" was 0.8% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" was 2.7% (similar to 2011).

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in good health in Reigate and Banstead decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Reigate and Banstead households, 15.7% rented privately in 2021, up from 12.9% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in nine households (11.5%) lived in socially rented housing, compared with 11.9% in 2011. The percentage of Reigate and Banstead households that owned their home (outright or with a mortgage or loan) decreased from 73.0% to 71.1%.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes in Reigate and Banstead (2.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 16.3% to 19.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Reigate and Banstead increased by 2.7 percentage points

Unpaid care in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 4.4% of Reigate and Banstead residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care was greater in Reigate and Banstead (3.1 percentage points) than across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Reigate and Banstead decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 7.5% of Reigate and Banstead residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 5.1% in 2011. The 2.5 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 84.4% of people in Reigate and Banstead identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 90.6% in 2011), while 3.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.2% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.6% in 2011 to 2.9% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 7.5% of usual residents in Reigate and Banstead identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 38.1% of Reigate and Banstead residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.3% in 2011. The rise of 11.8 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Reigate and Banstead. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 49.1% of people in Reigate and Banstead described themselves as Christian (down from 61.9%), while 6.0% did not state their religion (down from 7.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 38.1% of usual residents in Reigate and Banstead reported having "No religion"

Reigate and Banstead residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 122,700 Reigate and Banstead residents said they were born in England. This represented 81.3% of the local population. The figure has risen from just over 117,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 85.0% of Reigate and Banstead's population.

India was the next most represented, with just under 2,700 Reigate and Banstead residents reporting this country of birth (1.8%). This figure was up from around 1,300 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.9% of the population of Reigate and Banstead.

The number of Reigate and Banstead residents born in Scotland fell from around 2,100 in 2011 (1.5% of the local population) to around 1,800 in 2021 (1.2%).

In 2021, 81.3% of Reigate and Banstead residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 8.4% of Reigate and Banstead residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 6.7% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 1.1% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Reigate and Banstead that identified as "British only" increased from 18.2% to 57.8%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK in Reigate and Banstead (1.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Reigate and Banstead increased by 1.7 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Reigate and Banstead residents aged 16 years and over, 33.1% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 30.8% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in two people (50.6%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 51.7% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Reigate and Banstead that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.4% to 8.5%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%) than in Reigate and Banstead (2.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Reigate and Banstead increased by 2.3 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Reigate and Banstead residents aged 16 years and over, 61.3% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 63.0% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.4%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.6% in 2011. The percentage of retired Reigate and Banstead residents increased from 20.6% to 20.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed was greater in Reigate and Banstead (1.7 percentage points) than across the South East (1.3 percentage points, from 59.0% to 57.6%). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.8 percentage points, from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Reigate and Banstead decreased by 1.7 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 10.7% of Reigate and Banstead residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 9.7% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Reigate and Banstead (1.0 percentage points) than across the South East (0.5 percentage points, from 10.4% to 11.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Reigate and Banstead increased by 1.0 percentage points

Disability in Reigate and Banstead

In 2021, 5.5% of Reigate and Banstead residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 11 people (8.9%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.4% in 2011. The proportion of Reigate and Banstead residents who were not disabled increased from 85.2% to 85.6%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Reigate and Banstead (0.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Reigate and Banstead decreased by 0.9 percentage points
